alex: Kicking off a canary of NVIDIA driver 585 (kernel-compat build) to a small slice in us-west2 + ap-southeast1. First wave looks fine, but 3/20 nodes in ap-southeast1 failed to come up after reboot. They stay at the installer/boot stage.

sam_oncall: Which symptom? boot loop, kernel panic, or modprobe errors?

alex: Stuck during initramfs while trying to load drivers. Seen in serial console: `modprobe: FATAL: Module nvidia not found in directory /lib/modules/5.15.0-101-generic` but the filesystem actually contains `nvidia.ko` in a different path. DKMS post-install did something weird.

kevin: Can you paste the initramfs log snippet? Also did DKMS report success?

alex: Paste: ```
[    7.842103] initramfs: executing /sbin/modprobe -k nvidia
[    7.842107] modprobe: FATAL: Module nvidia not found in directory /lib/modules/5.15.0-101-generic
[    7.842109] nvhost: probe of 0000:00:04.0 failed with error -22
[    7.842110] kernel: rmmod: ERROR: Module nvidia is in use
```

alex: `dkms status` on the broken node shows: `nvidia,585: installed` but `ls -la /lib/modules/5.15.0-101-generic/kernel/drivers/video/` shows `nvidia.ko -> ../../../../extra/nvidia-585/nvidia.ko` (symlink pointing into package dir). The package dir exists, but `modprobe` can't resolve it during early initramfs because the symlink target isn't included in the initramfs.

priya: That explains initramfs failure. Was update-initramfs run in postinst? Maybe the package assumed dracut or different initramfs tooling. Which image builder are these nodes using?

alex: These nodes use our legacy provisioning image (custom cloud-init + update-initramfs). The driver package's postinst runs `dracut --regenerate` if it sees dracut, else it runs `update-initramfs -u`, but the DKMS package created module under `/usr/src/nvidia-585/` and symlinked to `/lib/modules/$(uname -r)/extra/` — in our image builder we don't include `/usr/src` contents in the initramfs. So the symlink resolves to a path not packaged.

mira: Is this limited to nodes with that specific kernel version? Any correlation with nodes that have custom kernel packages (we've got a subset with performance kernel)?

alex: Yes, all repro nodes are on `5.15.0-101-generic` with the performance-kernel patch applied. Non-performance nodes on the same release were fine because their initramfs packaging differs (we include extra/). So it's a packaging mismatch + DKMS placement.

sam_oncall: What's the immediate impact on capacity? Numbers?

alex: ap-southeast1 lost 3 GPU nodes => ~12% GPU capacity from that AZ. Scheduling fallback pushed jobs to us-west, increasing costs by ~18% in the last 2 hours. Some NCCL jobs timed out due to cross-region placement, saw `NCCL WARN NET/IB: Connection timed out`.

kevin: Deploy-bot, what was the rollout window?

deploy-bot: deploy event: user alex triggered `drivers/nvidia-585` canary at 2098765380. Target: 20 nodes in canary pool. Status: paused (manually) after 3 failures.

priya: Recommended mitigation: 1) Hold rollout (done), 2) Mark the 3 failed nodes for repro and snapshot, 3) Rollback canary to previous GA driver (560) for the rest of canary pool nodes, 4) Update preflight to check for symlink-resolvable modules in initramfs.

mira: Agree. Also we should add a preflight that runs `chroot /target update-initramfs -t -k $(uname -r)` or simply validate that `/lib/modules/$(uname -r)` contains direct object files (no external symlink targets).

alex: I'm preparing a rollback playbook. Plan: cordon & drain unaffected canary nodes, install driver 560 package from our cached repo, regenerate initramfs, reboot. For the 3 repro nodes, preserve disk and attach serial logs to a ticket.

sam_oncall: Will we need a scheduler override to avoid packing multi-GPU NCCL jobs into reduced capacity? We already saw cross-region fallback.

kevin: I'll patch the autoscaler to temporarily increase opportunistic burst in us-west to compensate and avoid cross-region NCCL placements. That will raise cost but keeps latency SLAs.

priya: Long-term fix ideas: (a) change DKMS packaging to copy modules instead of symlinking into /lib/modules, (b) ensure postinst always regenerates initramfs including any extra/ and /usr/src targets, (c) add a validation hook in our AMI builder to test a kernel module load/unload and `rmmod` to detect references.

alex: I'm filing ticket: https://redwood.internal/infra/ISSUE-1423 - includes repro nodes, serial logs, dkms status, and suggested remediation.

mira: Also add a test to our upgrade-canary pipeline to install driver package in a VM with performance-kernel applied and boot it in QEMU to catch initramfs resolution issues pre-rollout.

deploy-bot: action required: rollback requested by alex at 2098765450. Rolling remaining canary nodes to driver 560.

kevin: I'll run a targeted rollback, estimate about 14 minutes per node to install + rebuild initramfs + reboot. With 17 nodes remaining that's ~4 hours serially; will parallelize to 5 at a time to keep risk low (~1h30).

sam_oncall: Keep paging if any node fails to come back. Also tag impacted jobs and notify customers if any long-running jobs are evicted.

priya: After rollback, let's schedule a postmortem: root cause seems to be packaging assumption mismatch between DKMS + initramfs tools + our image builder. Also check kernel header package versions used when building DKMS module.

alex: TL;DR: canary paused, rollback in progress to 560, preserving repro nodes for investigation. Refs: runbook https://redwood.internal/runbooks/dkms-driver-failures and ISSUE-1423. Will update thread when rollback completes. :thumbsup:

mira: Thanks — and create a short note for capacity/cost ops so finance knows the temporary bump.

kevin: Noted, will send a quick summary to #finance.

sam_oncall: Acknowledge.

priya: adding a small checklist in ISSUE-1423 for the postmortem and remediation owners.

alex: rolling update: 8/17 nodes rolled back so far, no additional repros. ETA ~45m.

mira: copy. Keep monitoring NCCL job failures for the next 2 hours.

alex: rollback finished at 2098765599, canary pool stable on driver 560. Leaving the 3 repro nodes offline for analysis. Closing immediate incident.

sam_oncall: great work team, will capture incident summary in postmortems later. :party-parrot:
